standard.title: Recognise and communicate meaning
standard.description: with support, recognise and communicate meaning in the target language
standard.prior_knowledge: Foundation students are beginning formal schooling. Background language learners bring significant prior exposure to the target language through home, family and community — they can recognise spoken language, respond to familiar phrases, and communicate in informal home contexts. They have not yet engaged with the target language in a structured school setting, and have not used it for classroom routines, peer interaction, or formal communicative tasks.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and communicate meaning in the target language with support, using familiar phrases, gestures and formulaic expressions in classroom and personal interaction contexts.

nodes.label: Recognising and responding to familiar spoken language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise familiar spoken words, phrases and formulaic expressions in the target language and respond through gesture, action or single words.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond appropriately to at least three familiar classroom instructions or greetings in the target language through action, gesture or spoken word.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and respond to a range of familiar spoken expressions — greetings, instructions, questions about self — using gesture, action or brief spoken response; identify key words in songs, rhymes and short exchanges.
wider: Identify and distinguish familiar phrases across different tones or speakers — for example, recognising that the same greeting is used differently with teachers versus peers
Connect spoken words to visual or physical representations — labelling, pointing, or acting out responses to a broader range of classroom and daily-life phrases
nodes.hinge_reason: Recognising familiar spoken language is the entry condition for all communicative participation. Students who cannot identify and respond to spoken target language cannot engage in classroom routines, peer interaction, or any of the communicative tasks that follow across this descriptor and the year band.

response_modes.reason: Background learners bring varied and uneven prior exposure — some phrases are deeply familiar, others are not. Building a shared classroom repertoire of recognised expressions through songs, rhymes, routines and repeated spoken encounters ensures all students have a working set before productive communication tasks begin.

success_criteria: Responds correctly to at least three familiar spoken instructions or greetings through action, gesture or word
Identifies at least two familiar words or phrases when heard in a song, rhyme or spoken text

nodes.label: Using formulaic expressions in interaction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use familiar formulaic phrases to interact in simple classroom and social exchanges — greeting, thanking, requesting and responding.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two formulaic expressions appropriately in a real or play-based interaction context — for example, a greeting exchange or a request using a learned phrase.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of formulaic expressions across everyday interaction purposes — greeting, thanking, apologising, requesting, expressing likes and dislikes — with appropriate gesture and body language; participate in simple exchange routines with teacher and peers.
wider: Use learned expressions spontaneously in play-based and dramatic contexts — for example, a role-play shop, doctor or restaurant scenario — adapting phrases to the situation
Share familiar expressions with family or peers from outside the class — for example, teaching a greeting or song, demonstrating use across social contexts beyond the classroom

response_modes.reason: Formulaic expressions are context-bound at Foundation level — students who have only rehearsed a phrase in one context (e.g. a greeting with the teacher) may not transfer it to peer interaction or play. Varied interaction contexts — role-play, songs, games, paired exchanges — build the flexible use that productive communication requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Foundation background learners often have rich home-language repertoires that can be activated and extended through varied communicative contexts. Width investment here — particularly in play-based and family-connected tasks — builds on the authentic communicative experience students bring rather than treating them as beginners.
success_criteria: Uses at least two formulaic expressions appropriately in an interaction context without direct prompting
Demonstrates understanding of the communicative purpose of a phrase — for example, uses a greeting to initiate rather than respond, or uses a request phrase when needed

nodes.label: Communicating personal meaning with support
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can communicate simple personal meaning in the target language — sharing information about themselves, expressing preferences or needs — using modelled phrases and visual or spoken cues.
nodes.minimum_width: Communicate at least one piece of personal information (name, age, preference) in the target language using a modelled sentence or phrase, with support.
nodes.typical_width: Share personal information and express simple preferences and needs using modelled sentence structures; participate in brief personal introduction exchanges with teacher and peers; use target language alongside gesture and visual cues to convey meaning.
wider: Create a simple personal text — a self-portrait caption, greeting card or illustrated sentence — combining target language words or phrases with images to communicate personal meaning
Use target language to communicate in a brief structured exchange with a peer, drawing on both known phrases and new contexts introduced in the activity

response_modes.reason: Communicating personal meaning integrates recognition (node 1) and formulaic expression use (node 2) into a productive task that requires students to select and deploy language for a communicative purpose. The teaching investment is in creating genuine communicative conditions — real audiences, real purposes — rather than only rehearsed recitation.

success_criteria: Communicates at least one piece of personal information in the target language using a modelled phrase, with or without visual support
Participates in a brief personal exchange — at minimum, responding to a personal question — using target language
